answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A randomized audit samples completed work; if several identities are shown to share control or submit fabricated results, the protocol can slash their deposits and cap their influence by stake rather than by account count. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must lock real capital for every fake identity and risks losing it. The delta between expected rewards and audit losses matters; a terrace or grove of accounts offers no cheap shortcut.
